en: Despite these problems, there appeared to be no other way to establish paths of communication with Austronesian language speakers. Even if official interpreters could learn indigenous languages, they were not stationed in places where they might have been useful. According to the personnel rosters for the first year of the Pacification Office’s operation (1896), there were eight translators posted among its eleven stations.
The following year, the translator positions were all gone, although four of the 1896 translators remained as administrative assistants (
), now performing “routine duties and tasks to be determined by the station chief, including interpreting.”
In the late summer of 1897, one Pacification Office head reported in the
that even when translators were employed, communication was still difficult because they did not understand the local dialects very well.
The Pacification Office was dissolved the next year, and aborigine administration was moved to Section 3 of the new District Administrative Offices (
). As a rule, the
stations lacked translators altogether.
zh: 尽管有这些问题，似乎别无他法可与南岛语使用者建立沟通渠道。即便官方通译能学会原住民语言，他们也没有被派驻到可能派上用场的地方。据抚垦署启用的第一年（1896）的人事名册，其十一个站点共派驻八名通译。
次年，通译职位全部取消，尽管1896年的通译中有四人留任行政助理（shujiho，书记补），如今执行“日常事务与由站长决定的任务，包括传译”。
1897年夏末，一位抚垦署长在《读卖新闻》上报告，即便雇用了通译，沟通仍然困难，因为他们不太懂当地方言。
抚垦署于次年被撤销，理蕃行政移交给新设辨务署（Benmusho）第三课。一般而言，辨务署各站根本没有通译。

en: But without Japanese staffers trained in indigenous languages, wrote one pacification officer in 1898, Japan was doomed to rely upon the shady local men who cheated indigenes by plying them with booze. The local men also frustrated Japanese policy by trafficking contraband rifles.

One obvious measure to dispense with Japan’s reliance on interpreters, without relying on the fractious intercultural marriages, was formal language training for pacification officers and policemen. In March 1897, as a first step, the head of the Industrial Section in Taipei ordered Pacification Office heads to compile word lists and phrase books based on trading-post conversations, official meet and greets, and negotiations of camphor contracts with indigenes. The memorandum’s author wrote that indigenous languages had no historical affinities to Chinese or Japanese and that mastering them was difficult. The circular proposed systematic word collection and phonetic analysis with the cooperation of the Pacification Office. Materials started trickling in by October 1897.
zh: 但一位抚垦官员在1898年写道，若无受过原住民语言训练的日本职员，日本注定要依赖那些品行可疑的社丁——他们用酒灌原住民以行欺骗。社丁还贩运走私步枪，挫败日本政策。
要摆脱日本对通译的依赖、又不靠那些纷争不断的跨文化婚姻，一个显而易见的措施是对抚垦官员与警察进行正规语言训练。1897年3月，作为第一步，台北工业课长命各抚垦署长根据贸易站对话、官方会见以及与原住民谈判樟脑契约，编纂词汇表与会话手册。备忘录作者写道，原住民语言与汉语或日语没有历史亲缘关系，掌握它们很难。该通令提议在抚垦署配合下系统搜集词汇并进行语音分析。到1897年10月，材料开始零星送来。

en: However, as anthropologist Mio Yūko’s careful analysis of the manuscript copies of the responses reveals, the stacks of word lists and conversational phrases were made by linguistic amateurs, written down in katakana (a Japanese syllabary), and they ended up collecting dust in government offices. The ambitious project did not produce training manuals or textbooks, leaving the Japanese to learn indigenous languages through immersion.
zh: 然而，正如人类学家三尾裕子（Mio Yūko）对这些回复手稿抄本的细致分析所揭示，那一摞摞词汇表与会话短语出自语言业余人士之手，以片假名（一种日语音节文字）记写，最终在政府办公室里蒙尘。这项雄心勃勃的工程没有产出训练手册或教科书，使日本人只能靠沉浸式接触学习原住民语言。

en: To incentivize immersion learning, the so-called

(stipend) system was implemented. In this program, police officers and assistant policemen were given monthly pay supplements if they could pass language exams in Hok-lo, Hakka, or an Austronesian language.

The pay incentives for Han Taiwanese assistant patrolmen to learn Japanese succeeded. The Taiwan Government-General thus cultivated a cohort of Japanese-speaking Han Taiwanese to handle interpreting chores in the plains and ports. However, the stipend system was premised on the assumption that a comprehensive and fair exam could be administered in the target language. It is clear from the foregoing, however, that Japanese officials were not in possession of instructional materials or a language pedagogy that could produce examinations, examiners, and a curriculum for Austronesian languages.
zh: 为激励沉浸式学习，实施了所谓的津贴（kensho）制度。在该计划下，警官与巡查补若能通过福佬话、客家话或某种南岛语的考试，便可获得每月加薪津贴。
激励汉人台湾巡查补学习日语的加薪措施成功了。台湾总督府由此培养出一批会说日语的汉人台湾人，在平原与港口处理传译杂务。然而，津贴制度以一个假设为前提：能用目标语言施行全面而公平的考试。但从上文清楚可见，日本官员并不掌握能为南岛语产出考试、考官与课程的教学材料或语言教学法。

en: Therefore, an exception was made. The indigenous-language tests would consist of abbreviated interviews with Japanese district officials, who determined if a candidate understood an indigenous language sufficiently to “communicate and understand complex matters” and “relay orders without doing damage.” Examinees would be sorted into three categories of proficiency.
A set of 1907 regulations stated that exams for indigenous languages be limited to oral interviews. That same year,
(indigenous language) was officially defined as nine separate tongues: Atayal, Saisiyat, Bunun, Tsou, Tsarisen, Amis, Puyuma, Paiwan, and Yami.
zh: 因此作了例外处理。原住民语言考试将由日本地方官员主持简短面试，由他们判定考生是否充分掌握某种原住民语言，足以“沟通并理解复杂事务”、“传达命令而不致造成损害”。考生将被分为三个熟练等级。
1907年的一套规章规定，原住民语言考试限于口试。同年，蕃语（bango，即原住民语言）被正式定义为九种独立语言：泰雅、赛夏、布农、邹、鲁凯（Tsarisen）、阿美、卑南、排湾、雅美。

en: The practical application of government ethnologist Inō Kanori’s taxonomy (see

) had important long-term consequences. There are many more Austronesian languages in Taiwan than the nine listed above. As Inō’s colleague and rival ethnologist Mori Ushinosuke observed at the time, Inō’s taxonomy lumped dissimilar languages together, while it split similar languages into separate categories. Mori himself advocated a sixfold classification that fused Saisiyat with Atayal and grouped Puyuma, Tsarisen (Rukai), and Paiwan together, based on his own research as the Meiji era’s most dogged survey ethnologist of Taiwan. Despite Mori’s reservations, however, these nine groups became census categories, museum labels, and place-names on ethnic maps. As inscribed ethnonyms, they were carried forward with considerable institutional momentum into the late twentieth century (with the exception of Tsarisen, which essentially became Rukai). Until indigenous activists themselves met with some success in revising the taxonomy in the twenty-first century, these nine language groups constituted the building blocks of indigenous Taiwan’s second-order geobody.
zh: 政府民族学家伊能嘉矩分类法（见

）的实际应用，产生了重要的长期后果。台湾的南岛语远不止上述九种。正如伊能的同僚兼对手、民族学家森丑之助当时所观察，伊能的分类法把不同的语言归并在一起，又把相似的语言拆成不同类别。森本人主张一种六分法，把赛夏并入泰雅，把卑南、鲁凯（Tsarisen）、排湾归为一组，依据的是他作为明治时代最锲而不舍的台湾调查民族学家的自身研究。然而，尽管森有所保留，这九个群体还是成了人口普查类别、博物馆标签与族群地图上的地名。作为被铭刻的族名，它们带着相当大的制度惯性延续到二十世纪末（原称 Tsarisen 的一项除外，其名称基本由“鲁凯”取代）。直到二十一世纪原住民行动者自身在修订分类法上取得若干成功之前，这九个语言群体构成了原住民台湾“二阶地理体”的基石。

en: On July 27, 1909, police headquarters circulated another memorandum urging colonial police stationed in the northern districts to learn Taiwanese and indigenous languages. The Yilan district station employed three instructors in the office and another at a garrison. At other locations, however, no qualified instructors could be found, so the men were reduced to studying word lists on their own. One district head noted that lack of contact with Atayal people for actual practice hindered progress. The Xinzhu station chief claimed that most of his men could say a few words in an indigenous language but could not conduct everyday conversations. The best he could do was provide nonsystematic practice for the policemen under his command with indigenous mercenaries or the indigenous wives of Japanese policemen.
zh: 1909年7月27日，警察本部下发另一份备忘录，敦促派驻北方各区的殖民警察学习台湾语与原住民语言。宜兰区站在署内雇了三名教习，另在驻军处雇了一名。然而在其他地方，找不到合格教习，于是这些人只能自行研读词汇表。一位区长指出，缺乏与泰雅人实际练习的接触阻碍了进步。新竹站长声称，他手下大多数人能用原住民语言说几个词，却无法进行日常对话。他所能做的至多，是让麾下巡查与原住民雇佣兵或日本警察的原住民妻子进行非系统练习。

en: It is not surprising that conversation partners for uniformed Japanese and Taiwanese officials were scarce in 1909. We saw in chapter 1 how Kondō Katsusaburō and Iwan Robao (or possibly other informants to the Japanese government) orchestrated a trap for Hōgō- and Paalan-village Tgdaya (Wushe) men, who lost most of their weapons and warriors on a single day, on October 5, 1903. After their defeat, emissaries from Wushe notified a local police office that the severity of the trade embargo had inflicted suffering, and they offered to supply troops and porters to help build a guardline. The Taiwan Government-General kept Hōgō waiting. They finally sent negotiators in late 1905. Kondō Katsusaburō then acted as the go-between to orchestrate Wushe’s surrender in 1906. In order to resume trade, the Paalan and Hōgō headmen allowed the government-general to build a guardline path to the summit of Shoucheng Dashan, just below its 2,420-meter peak. This commanding height overlooked dozens of settlements of strategic interest in and around Wushe.
To avoid being shot on sight, the Wushe-area men were told to bring Japanese flags to the Kasumigaseki station and check in before hunting in the area.

From this new section of guardline, which cut the Tgdaya villages off from the trade hub of Puli, the government-general was able to encircle the Atayal, Truku, and Sediq tribes north of Wushe in subsequent campaigns.

For brokering the surrender ceremony at the Kasumigaseki station, Kondō was awarded seventy yen for meritorious service. This was an extraordinary bonus. At this time, the top cash award for ranking inspectors was only sixty yen.
zh: 1909年，身着制服的日本与台湾官员缺乏会话伙伴，这并不奇怪。第一章已见，近藤胜三郎与伊娃莉·罗拔俄（或可能是日本政府的其他线人）如何为荷戈与芭兰村的德固达雅（雾社）男子设下陷阱，使他们在1903年10月5日一天之内损失了大部分武器与战士。败北之后，雾社的使者通知当地警察署，严厉的贸易禁运已造成苦难，并提出提供兵员与挑夫协助修筑隘勇线。台湾总督府让荷戈一直等待。他们最终于1905年末派出谈判者。近藤胜三郎随后充当居间人，促成雾社1906年的归顺。为恢复贸易，芭兰与荷戈头目允许总督府修筑一条通往守城大山（Shoucheng Dashan）山顶的隘勇线路径，抵达其海拔2,420米的峰顶下方。这一制高点俯瞰雾社及周边数十个具有战略意义的聚落。
为避免被就地射杀，雾社一带男子被告知，在该地狩猎前须携日本旗到霞关站报到。
从这段新隘勇线——它把德固达雅各村社与贸易枢纽埔里切断——总督府得以在后续征伐中包围雾社以北的泰雅、德路固、赛德克各社。
因居间促成霞关站的归顺仪式，近藤获70日元军功奖金。这是一笔非凡的奖金。当时，高阶警部的最高现金奖赏不过60日元。

en: Perhaps hoping to reproduce the 1906 breakthrough attributed to Kondō Katsusaburō, who was married to Iwan Robao of Paalan, Police Bureau head Ōtsu Rinpei urged the government to actively encourage, instead of merely tolerate, mixed marriages between low-ranking Japanese officers and indigenous women from chiefly lineages.
zh: 或许是想复制1906年那归功于近藤胜三郎（他娶了芭兰的伊娃莉·罗拔俄）的突破，警察部长大津麟平敦促政府积极鼓励、而非仅仅容忍低阶日本警官与出自酋长世系的原住民女性之间的通婚。

en: THE POLITICAL MARRIAGES UNDER SAKUMA SAMATA’S ADMINISTRATION
zh: 佐久间左马太施政下的政治婚姻

en: Following the Russo-Japanese War (1904–05), Governor-General Sakuma Samata’s administration (1906–15) accelerated the policy of military conquest over the Atayal villages that had refused to surrender their rifles and sovereignty during the previous decade of colonial rule. Although Wushe had formally submitted in 1906, many of the tribes farther upland and inland still remained defiant. Sakuma pledged to break the resistance of the northern tribes once and for all by extending the heavily armed guardline to the heart of Atayal country to encompass Xalut (which subsumed Masitoban), Truku, and Toda (see
zh: 日俄战争（1904—1905）之后，佐久间左马太总督的施政（1906—1915）加快了军事征服的政策，矛头指向那些在此前十年殖民统治中拒不交出步枪与主权的泰雅族村落。虽然雾社已于1906年正式归顺，但更靠山地、更靠内陆的许多部落依然桀骜不驯。佐久间誓言要一举击破北部部落的抵抗，把重武装的隘勇线推进到泰雅族地区的腹地，将白狗（其下包含马西托班）、德路固与都达囊括其中（见

en: Sakuma’s right-hand man on indigenous policy, Police Bureau chief Ōtsu Rinpei, inspected the forward posts of the guardline in spring 1907. His report proposed to remedy the alarming interpreter situation with a “political-marriage” policy:
zh: 佐久间在原住民事务上的左膀右臂、警务局长大津麟平，于1907年春视察了隘勇线的前沿哨所。他的报告提出以一项“政治婚姻”政策来补救令人忧虑的通译状况：

en: I have sensed an extreme paucity of indigenous-language translators at every installation on my tour. This being the case, it is not difficult to imagine that many, many more translators will be necessary as we bring the indigenes within the fold of government. I need not mention that success in managing the indigenes hinges upon the ability of our translators.... The quickest route to cultivating translators would be to give occasional financial assistance to the appropriate men and have them officially marry
zh: 我在巡视途中，感到每一处设施中原住民语通译都极度匮乏。既然如此，不难想见，当我们把原住民纳入政府管辖之内时，将需要多得多的通译。毋庸赘言，管理原住民的成败系于我们通译的能力……培养通译最快捷的途径，莫过于对合适的人选偶尔给予经济资助，并让他们正式娶蕃婦为妻。

en: [We] recognize that such marriages can cause trouble because indigenes... will say that such marriages are unfair and benefit only the villages or lineages of the

’s new husband. By the same token, if the Japanese husband is rotated to another post and abandons his wife, it will offend indigenous sentiment. Nonetheless, our present lack of translators is troubling. Because marriage to an indigenous woman will raise living expenses, occasional moneys should be provided for the low-ranking men who cannot afford it.
zh: 〔我们〕认识到，这类婚姻可能惹出麻烦，因为原住民……会说这种婚姻不公平，只惠及蕃婦新夫所属的村落或宗族。同样，倘若日本丈夫被调往别处任职而抛弃妻子，也会触犯原住民的情感。尽管如此，我们眼下通译的短缺仍令人苦恼。由于娶原住民女子会增加生活开销，对那些无力承担的低阶人员，应偶尔拨给款项。

en: In August 1908Ōtsu commissioned Kondō to secure Wushe allies in order to add another spur to the system of guardlines already in place. Kondō himself initially demurred but then reconsidered when Ōtsu offered him a land grant of thirty hectares near the Kasumigaseki police station outside Puli. In October Kondō found allies in the settlements of Hōgō (headman Aui Nukan) and Mehebu (headman Ludao Bai), two Tgdaya groups who considered Truku and Toda enemies.
According to Kondō, Ludao Bai and Aui Nukan demanded that he and his younger brother Gisaburō (see
) take wives in Wushe to seal the bargain. Accordingly, Kondō paid the price of one pig to Paalan’s chief to ratify his “divorce” from Iwan Robao to pave the way for his second marriage.
zh: 1908年8月，大津委派近藤去争取雾社的盟友，以便在既有的隘勇线系统上再加一道支线。近藤起初推辞，但当大津提出在埔里城外霞关警察站附近授予他三十公顷土地时，他改变了主意。10月，近藤在荷戈（头目阿乌伊·努坎）与马赫坡（头目鲁道·拜）两处聚落找到了盟友，这两个德固达雅群体视德路固与都达为敌。
据近藤所述，鲁道·拜与阿乌伊·努坎要求他和弟弟仪三郎（见
）在雾社娶妻，以坐实这笔交易。为此，近藤向芭兰的头目交出一头猪，请其认可他与伊娃莉·罗拔俄的“离异”，为他的第二次婚姻铺路。

The photographer, Mori Ushinosuke, attested to Kondō’s linguistic prowess in Truku and credited him with helping to defeat the Truku pictured here. Note the oilcan in the foreground: a bamboo indigenous drinking vessel is resting on top. Mori Ushinosuke, ed.,

en: In January 1909 the brothers Kondō were married to Obin Nukan and Chiwas Ludao. In late February, soon after the formalization of the alliance by marriage, Kondō Katsusaburō led some 654 Wushe warriors in the general attack on Toda and Truku, which was successfully concluded by March 1909.

The official report states that Wushe drew the Taiwan Government-General into a local feud by blaming Toda for recent attacks on the Japanese guardline. The report’s authors were skeptical of the charges against Toda but went along because they thought it expedient to use Wushe’s manpower to gain a strategic foothold in difficult terrain. In addition to Kondō’s 654 Wushe (Tgdaya) allies, who apparently acted as laborers, the government fielded 580 fighting men for the climactic attack on Toda.

These maneuvers secured more commanding heights for Japanese cannon and mortars as well as strategic passes for communication, which allowed the government-general to effectively hem in the Sediq territory from all sides.
zh: 1909年1月，近藤兄弟分别与奥宾·努坎和奇瓦斯·鲁道成婚。2月下旬，在婚姻正式缔结盟约后不久，近藤胜三郎率领约654名雾社战士，参与了对都达与德路固的总攻，此役于1909年3月顺利结束。
官方报告称，雾社把近期对日本隘勇线的袭击归咎于都达，从而将台湾总督府拖入了一场地方仇杀。报告的作者对针对都达的指控心存怀疑，但仍顺势而为，因为他们认为利用雾社的人力在险峻地形中取得战略立足点是权宜之计。除了近藤那654名显然充当劳力的雾社（德固达雅）盟友之外，政府还投入了580名战斗人员，用于对都达的决定性一击。
这些调动为日军的大炮与迫击炮夺取了更多制高点，也拿下了用于通讯的战略隘口，使总督府得以从四面八方有效地把赛德克族的领土围困起来。

en: As an eldest son and a future

(household head), Kondō Katsusaburō expected to secure his Japanese family’s future by obtaining a large, government-registered farm near Puli for the care of his aged father, per Ōtsu Rinpei’s promise in August 1908. Indeed, Kondō’s father, who had immigrated to Taiwan by this time, passed away in March 1909, leaving Kondō legally responsible for the care of his mother, younger brothers and sisters, and a number of nieces. Kondō spent the years 1909 through 1916 pressing claims for the promised acreage while continuing to accept government commissions as a guide and interpreter.
zh: 作为长子、未来的户主（koshu），近藤胜三郎指望依照大津麟平1908年8月的许诺，在埔里附近取得一大片经政府登记的农田，以赡养年迈的父亲，从而保障自己日本家庭的未来。事实上，此时已移居台湾的近藤之父于1909年3月去世，使近藤在法律上负有赡养母亲、弟弟妹妹以及若干侄辈的责任。1909年至1916年间，近藤一边不断追索许诺的土地，一边继续接受政府委派，充当向导与通译。

en: As the years wore on, his patron Ōtsu Rinpei returned to Japan; other officials familiar with Kondō’s case left Nantou Prefecture. Finally, Wushe district police inspector Kondō Shōsaburō (no relation) deeded the land to his own relative, preempting Katsusaburō’s claim. This perceived slight angered Katsusaburō’s younger brother Gisaburō to the boiling point, according to Katsusaburō’s testimony. In 1916 Gisaburō tendered his resignation in Taipei but was instead transferred out of Wushe to a new post in Hualian District at Pushige.
zh: 随着岁月流逝，他的恩主大津麟平返回了日本；其他熟悉近藤案情的官员也离开了南投厅。最终，雾社地区的警部近藤庄三郎（与近藤胜三郎并无亲属关系）把那块土地过户给了自己的亲戚，抢先占去了胜三郎的申索。据胜三郎的证词，这一被视为轻慢的举动把弟弟仪三郎激怒到了极点。1916年，仪三郎在台北递交辞呈，却未被批准，反而被调离雾社，转往花莲厅璞石阁的新岗位。

en: Sixteen-year-old Kondō Gisaburō had come to Taiwan in 1901. Gisaburō worked his way up through the ranks to become a sergeant in the indigenous-territory police by the time of his infamous transfer, thanks to his facility with the Sediq dialects spoken near Wushe. Igarashi Ishimatsu, a Japanese official of long experience in Wushe, recalled Gisaburō as a companionate husband to Chiwas Ludao and a figure of local respect. Igarashi claimed that Chiwas’s devotion to Gisaburō allowed the Japanese to squelch an uprising by Xalut and Salamao in 1913. Overhearing the plan from her brother Mona Ludao, Chiwas alerted Gisaburō, who in turn sounded the alarm and averted disaster for the Japanese.
Such timely intelligence is all that Ōtsu Rinpei could have hoped for when he called for political marriages back in 1907. However, this success story would be short-lived.
zh: 十六岁的近藤仪三郎于1901年来到台湾。凭借对雾社附近所用赛德克方言的娴熟，仪三郎一路晋升，到那次声名狼藉的调动之时，已成为原住民领土警察中的一名巡查部长。在雾社任职多年的日本官员五十岚石松回忆说，仪三郎是奇瓦斯·鲁道体贴的丈夫，也是当地受人敬重的人物。五十岚声称，正是奇瓦斯对仪三郎的忠诚，使日本人得以挫败白狗与萨拉茅于1913年筹划的起义。奇瓦斯从兄长莫那·鲁道处偶然听到了计划，便提醒仪三郎，后者随即发出警报，为日本人避免了一场灾难。
这类及时的情报，正是大津麟平1907年呼吁政治婚姻时所能指望的全部。然而，这段成功故事却好景不长。

en: After Gisaburō’s 1916 transfer to Pushige, he never returned, leaving Chiwas bereft. She eventually remarried a local man but was never compensated with death benefits, nor was she given a sinecure, as was done with other abandoned wives.
Kondō Katsusaburō recalled that Chiwas had not been entered into Gisaburō’s
(household registry), making it impossible for the elder Kondō to file a claim on Chiwas’s behalf.
zh: 1916年仪三郎调往璞石阁之后，便再未回来，留下奇瓦斯孤苦无依。她最终改嫁了当地一名男子，却从未像其他被抛弃的妻子那样获得抚恤金，也未得到一份闲职。
近藤胜三郎回忆说，奇瓦斯并未被登入仪三郎的户籍（koseki），使得兄长近藤胜三郎无法代奇瓦斯提出申索。

en: THE TAISHŌ-PERIOD POLITICAL MARRIAGES
zh: 大正时期的政治婚姻

en: From 1909 to 1914, Sakuma Samata’s “five-year plan to control the aborigines” (gokanen keikaku riban jigyō) brought most of Atayal country under direct colonial rule. When the temporary organ established to administer Sakuma’s five-year plan (the Bureau of Aboriginal Affairs) was disbanded in July 1915, the Taiwan Government-General declared victory in the north.

Thereafter, the indigenous territory was governed by Japanese police officers who “possessed the power of life and death” over their colonial subjects. The indigenous-district police were charged with peacekeeping, educational, and medical functions. They became the eyes, ears, hands, and feet of the Taiwan Government-General in the lands under “special administration.” Unlike their predecessors, who lived near trading posts or in border towns, Japan’s new “aborigine hands” would reside among the tribes and villages that they governed. As salaried officials (in contrast to
), they would take direct orders from their superiors and transmit these orders to the “submitted tribes.”
zh: 1909年至1914年，佐久间左马太的“理蕃五年计划”（gokanen keikaku riban jigyō）把泰雅族地区的大部分置于殖民直接统治之下。1915年7月，为推行佐久间五年计划而设立的临时机构（蕃务本署）解散时，台湾总督府宣布在北方取得了胜利。
此后，原住民领土由对其殖民臣民“握有生杀大权”的日本警察官员治理。原住民地区的警察负有维持治安、教育与医疗的职能。他们成了台湾总督府在“特别行政”土地上的眼、耳、手、足。与那些住在贸易站附近或边界市镇的前辈不同，日本新的“蕃通”将居住在他们所治理的部落与村社之中。作为领薪的官员（与通事相对），他们直接听命于上级，并把这些命令传达给“归顺部落”。

en: Two particularly well-known Japanese-indigene marriages, both initiated to advance the guardline in Atayal country, survived into an era that saw increased surveillance and conscripted labor. One of these marriages ended in 1925 with the sacking of Shimoyama Jihei after a drunken altercation with his superior officer, the other in 1930 with the killing of Sazuka Aisuke in the Wushe uprising.
zh: 有两桩格外知名的日本人与原住民的婚姻，都是为了推进泰雅族地区的隘勇线而缔结的，它们一直存续到一个监视加剧、劳役征发的时代。其中一桩于1925年终结——下山治平因醉酒后与上级军官争执而被解职；另一桩于1930年终结——佐塚爱祐在雾社起义中被杀。

en: Shizuoka native Shimoyama Jihei arrived in Taiwan in 1907 as a young army veteran, two years before Sazuka’s arrival in 1909. During Sakuma’s five-year campaign, the Malepa dispatch station was overrun and its staff wiped out. To reestablish control, the Nantou District head of indigenous affairs sent Shimoyama to run things, after ordering him to marry Pixo Doleh, the daughter of Malepa’s headman. According to Pixo’s niece, Malepa assented to the marriage out of economic desperation to obtain needed patronage and rifles.

According to their son Hajime, Pixo became proficient at Japanese conversation. Shimoyama, on the other hand, could not speak Atayal. Pixo bore him two sons and two daughters. Shimoyama’s other betrothed, Shizuoka native Katsumata Nakako, arrived in Puli after he and Pixo had started their Malepa family. Nakako also began to bear Shimoyama’s children. For a time, Shimoyama shuttled between Puli and Malepa. No longer able to afford two households, he finally moved his Japanese family to Malepa. Pixo Doleh, the daughter and sister of local headmen in a fiercely monogamous society, was humiliated.
zh: 静冈人下山治平于1907年以年轻退伍军人的身份来到台湾，比1909年抵达的佐塚早了两年。在佐久间的五年征伐期间，马赫坡分遣所被攻陷，所内人员被尽数歼灭。为重建控制，南投厅蕃务负责人派下山前去主持局面，并先命令他娶马赫坡头目之女贝克·道雷为妻。据贝克的侄女说，马赫坡是出于经济上的绝望、为获取所需的庇护与步枪才同意这门婚事的。
据他们的儿子始说，贝克后来能熟练地用日语会话。下山则相反，不会说泰雅语。贝克为他生了两子两女。下山的另一位未婚妻、静冈人胜又仲子，是在他与贝克已在马赫坡成家之后才来到埔里的。仲子也开始为下山生儿育女。有一段时间，下山在埔里与马赫坡之间来回奔波。最终他无力再供养两个家庭，便把日本家庭迁到了马赫坡。贝克·道雷身为当地头目的女儿与姐妹，又处在一个严格奉行一夫一妻制的社会里，深感屈辱。

en: Shimoyama’s open display of contempt for Atayal sensibilities came to the attention of Neng’gao district commander (

) Akinaga Nagakichi in 1925. One oral history claims that Akinaga was tipped off by a disgruntled Atayal youth. In any event, Akinaga broached the delicate issue of bigamy in front of assembled Malepa men. Shimoyama retorted that Pixo’s relatives had consented to this arrangement. Besides, an angered Shimoyama replied, he had been assured that he could break off the political marriage to Pixo after three years’ time, even if there were children. For his part, Akinaga took umbrage at being contradicted publicly by a subaltern. Tempers flared. Shimoyama challenged Akinaga by grabbing his lapels. Akinaga then threw Shimoyama down on a table. Shimoyama was dismissed for insubordination the next day, a fact that demonstrated clearly that the government-general believed it could handle affairs in Malepa without him. Although his abrupt departure left Pixo bitter, Shimoyama secured a job for her at a Wushe infirmary at a salary of forty yen per month before he left. Nonetheless, Shimoyama’s son Hajime recalled that his mother was never entered into Shimoyama’s family register (

) as a legally recognized wife. Nonetheless, due to Pixo’s high status in local society and official concerns about the ramifications of mistreating a headman’s daughter, Shimoyama was not able to treat her as a disposable concubine.
zh: 下山公然蔑视泰雅人感受的举动，于1925年引起了能高郡守秋永长吉的注意。一份口述史称，是一名心怀不满的泰雅青年向秋永告的密。无论如何，秋永当着聚集的马赫坡男子的面，挑明了重婚这个棘手问题。下山反驳说，贝克的亲属已同意这种安排。他还气冲冲地回敬道，当初有人向他保证，三年之后即便有了孩子，他也可以解除与贝克的政治婚姻。秋永则因被一名下属当众顶撞而恼羞成怒。双方火气上涌。下山抓住秋永的衣襟向他挑衅。秋永随即把下山摔倒在一张桌子上。次日，下山以抗命为由被免职，这一事实清楚地表明，总督府自信没有他也能处理马赫坡的事务。尽管他的突然离去令贝克心怀怨愤，下山在离开前还是为她在雾社一家诊疗所谋得了一份月薪四十日元的工作。然而，下山的儿子始回忆说，母亲从未作为法律承认的妻子被登入下山的户籍（koseki）。不过，由于贝克在当地社会地位很高，官方又顾虑虐待头目之女可能带来的后果，下山并不能把她当作可以随意抛弃的妾来对待。

en: Nagano Prefecture native Sazuka Aisuke (1886–1930), unable to abide impoverished country life in Japan’s “snow country,” fled to Taiwan via Tokyo one January morning in 1909 with money stolen from his father.

Five years later, as combined police, army, and navy forces bombarded resistant villages near Hualian Harbor in the last spasms of Sakuma’s “campaign to end all campaigns,” Sazuka married Yawai Taimu, the daughter of an Atayal headman in Masitoban, just north of Wushe.
zh: 长野县人佐塚爱祐（1886—1930）无法忍受日本“雪国”贫困的乡村生活，于1909年1月的一个早晨，带着从父亲那里偷来的钱，经东京逃往台湾。
五年后，正当警察、陆军与海军联合部队炮击花莲港附近顽抗的村落、为佐久间“毕其功于一役的征伐”作最后挣扎之际，佐塚娶了亚娃伊·泰目——雾社正北方马西托班一位泰雅头目的女儿。

en: Sazuka’s wife, Yawai, was remembered as one who spoke proper Japanese and worked harder than other Atayal women to assimilate to Japanese customs.

As one postmortem account of the Wushe Rebellion put it, Yawai married outside her local society only to be mistrusted by her fellow Atayal. She was also looked down upon by Japanese colonists for being a “savage.”

In a word, Sazuka and Yawai were representative outcasts of empire. One left the bleak prospects of Nagano behind to seek fortune in a colonial periphery, while the other was cast out by her father to shore up his position as a local headman.
zh: 佐塚的妻子亚娃伊，被人记作一位说一口地道日语、比其他泰雅女子更卖力地融入日本习俗的人。
正如一份关于雾社起义的事后记述所言，亚娃伊嫁到了本地社会之外，却只落得被泰雅同胞猜疑。她又因身为“生番”而遭日本殖民者轻视。
一言以蔽之，佐塚与亚娃伊正是帝国弃民的典型。一个抛下长野黯淡的前程，到殖民边缘地带去寻求发迹；另一个则被父亲嫁到本社之外，为的是巩固他自己的地方头目地位。

en: For his willingness to persevere in aborigine country, Sazuka was finally made chief of the Wushe branch station on March 31, 1930.

Wushe was an administrative center and showpiece for Japanese policies vis-à-vis the northern Taiwan Indigenous Peoples, a real step up from isolated Masitoban. There were eleven settlements under his new watch, and Wushe boasted a post office, schools, hot-springs inns, trading posts, and dormitories for students and government workers. Although it was a promotion, the reassignment to Wushe turned out to be Sazuka’s death sentence. Because of their roots in Masitoban, Yawai and Sazuka were viewed suspiciously in Wushe. Residents in Wushe’s villages were Sediq Tgdaya, who spoke a different language than Masitoban Atayals. Shimoyama Hajime recalled that Sediq visitors to Atayalic Malepa spoke Japanese with their hosts, since Sediq and Atayal were mutually unintelligible.

In the Xalut settlements of Malepa and Masitoban, Sazuka relied upon his wife’s Masitoban networks for local knowledge and, to some extent, for his legitimacy as a leader for some two decades. His linguistic facility and political experience in these former posts, however, provided Sazuka with little useful intelligence in the new setting. On the contrary, Sazuka’s affiliation with a non-Sediq Atayal—his wife, Yawai Taimu—and her father inclined Tgdaya residents within his jurisdiction to accuse Sazuka of favoritism toward Xalut peoples. They expected Sazuka and Yawai to exact vengeance against Tgdaya peoples in relation to recent intra-indigenous (though state-aided) violence.

And although Ōtsu Rinpei thought low-ranking rural policemen such as Sazuka could maintain bicultural households on their modestly supplemented salaries, Sazuka was an infamous embezzler, who was known to withhold pay and salt it away for his personal use. After his death in the rebellion, it was discovered that he had amassed ¥2,000 in a savings account and ¥20,000 in cash.
zh: 由于佐塚甘愿在蕃地坚守，他终于在1930年3月31日被任命为雾社分遣所所长。

雾社是行政中心，也是日本对北台湾原住民政策的样板，比孤立的马西托班着实高了一级。他新管辖之下有十一处聚落，雾社还设有邮局、学校、温泉旅馆、贸易站，以及供学生与政府职员使用的宿舍。虽然这是一次升迁，调往雾社却成了佐塚的催命符。由于根在马西托班，亚娃伊与佐塚在雾社受到猜疑。雾社各村的居民是赛德克族德固达雅人，所说的语言与马西托班的泰雅人不同。下山始回忆说，到泰雅语区的马赫坡作客的赛德克人，与主人交谈时用的是日语，因为赛德克语与泰雅语彼此无法互通。

在马赫坡与马西托班这两处白狗聚落，佐塚依靠妻子的马西托班人脉获取地方知识，并在某种程度上借此确立自己作为领导者的正当性，如此约二十年。然而，他在这些旧岗位上的语言便利与政治经验，在新环境中却几乎提供不了有用的情报。恰恰相反，佐塚与一名非赛德克的泰雅人——他的妻子亚娃伊·泰目——及其父亲的关联，使他辖区内的德固达雅居民倾向于指责佐塚偏袒白狗人。他们料想，佐塚与亚娃伊会为了近期原住民内部的暴力事件报复德固达雅人，尽管这些冲突得到殖民政府的助推。
而且，尽管大津麟平认为像佐塚这样低阶的乡村警察靠略有补贴的薪水就能维持双文化家庭，佐塚却是个臭名昭著的贪污者，惯于克扣薪饷、私吞自用。他在起义中死后，人们发现他已在一个储蓄账户里攒下2000日元，另有现金20000日元。

en: Shimoyama Jihei’s ignominious firing and Sazuka Aisuke’s violent demise can be considered the final blows to a system of rule predicated on a gender division of labor for cross-cultural communication that dated back to early Qing times. In this system, locally embedded women, as the daughters of headmen or local indigenous notables, were either adopted or married into outsider families to act as buffers between politically separated but economically linked social formations. The men in this equation—be they Han merchants, settlers, or officials, or Japanese policemen or trading-post operators—capitalized on their wives’ bilingualism and local kin networks to make a go of it on the so-called savage border. In hindsight, it is clear that this ad hoc arrangement was perhaps adequate for maintaining a certain volume of cross-border trade or for gathering military intelligence for short-term expeditions. But intercultural marriages fell far short of providing a mechanism to consolidate a stable system of outsider rule among the Sediq, Atayal, and Truku peoples of northern Taiwan.
zh: 下山治平不光彩的被解职与佐塚爱祐遭杀害，可以视为对一套统治体制的最后打击——这套体制建立在跨文化沟通的性别分工之上，其渊源可追溯到清初。在这一体制中，深嵌于地方的女子，作为头目或地方原住民显要的女儿，或被收养、或嫁入外来者家庭，充当政治上是分离、经济上却相连的各社会形态之间的缓冲。处于这一安排中的男子——无论是汉人商人、移民或官员，还是日本警察或贸易站经营者——都利用妻子的双语能力与地方亲属网络，在所谓的“生番界”上谋生立足。事后看来，这种权宜安排或许足以维持一定规模的跨境贸易，或为短期征伐搜集军事情报。但跨文化婚姻远远未能提供一种机制，以在台湾的赛德克、泰雅与德路固诸族中巩固一套稳定的外来者统治体制。

en: According to statistics compiled by Kitamura Kae, twenty-nine Japanese policemen stationed in the special administrative district were proficient in an Atayalic language circa 1930, to rule over hundreds of settlements—many of them still hostile. According to Shimoyama Hajime, the son of Pixo and Jihei, the language barrier forced Japanese policemen to use blows instead of admonishments. Hajime extrapolated from his father’s beatings to hypothesize that generalized physical abuse was a long-term cause of the Wushe uprising. In an interview years after the fact, Hajime even wondered if better language skills among the Japanese police could have averted the slaughter that took place on October 27, 1930.
zh: 据北村嘉惠汇编的统计，约1930年，派驻特别行政区的日本警察中，只有二十九人精通一门泰雅语，却要治理数百处聚落——其中许多仍怀敌意。据贝克与治平之子下山始说，语言障碍迫使日本警察用拳脚代替告诫。始从父亲打人的做法推而广之，提出普遍的肢体虐待是雾社起义的一个长期成因。在事发多年后的一次访谈中，始甚至设想，倘若日本警察的语言能力更好些，是否就能避免1930年10月27日发生的那场屠杀。

en: TEACHING JAPANESE TO INDIGENOUS PEOPLES
zh: 向原住民教授日语

en: As Atayalic language competence among Japanese policemen declined in the 1920s, the Japanese language skill of indigenes was on the rise. The formal instruction of indigenous peoples in Japanese language was consonant with the generalized imperial impulse to diffuse national culture outward. It also aimed to cultivate a corps of interpreters whose loyalty was directed toward the state rather than their Taiwanese in-laws or private trading houses. While this project did not bear fruit in time to prevent the Wushe uprising, it represented the centerpiece of Japan’s assimilation policies toward indigenes.
zh: 1920年代，随着日本警察的泰雅语能力下降，原住民的日语水平却在上升。对原住民进行正式的日语教学，与帝国向外传播国民文化的普遍冲动相一致。它也旨在培养一支通译队伍，使其忠诚指向国家，而非指向他们的台湾姻亲或私人商行。虽然这一工程未能及时结出果实以阻止雾社起义，它却代表了日本对原住民同化政策的核心。

en: In 1896, soon after establishing itself in Taipei, the Taiwan Government-General established fourteen Japanese-language training institutes (kokugo denshūjo) throughout the island. Older students took crash courses in language and basic arithmetic to clerk and translate for the government. Younger students, as objects of the regime’s “attraction policy,” studied “written Chinese, geography, history, singing and gymnastics.”
The Hengchun walled city institute in southern Taiwan served a mixed population of “acculturated indigenes” (
) and Han students. Nearby, an annex school (bunkyōba) was built in Tuilasok; it was the first government school for indigenes.
zh: 1896年，台湾总督府在台北立足后不久，便在全岛设立了十四所国语传习所（kokugo denshūjo）。年长的学生上语言与基础算术的速成班，以便为政府充当文书与翻译。年幼的学生作为政权“笼络政策”的对象，学习“汉文、地理、历史、唱歌与体操”。
南台湾恒春城内的传习所，服务于“熟蕃”（jukuban）与汉人学生混杂的人群。附近，猪朥束建起了一所分校场（bunkyōba）；它是第一所官办原住民学校。

en: The Paiwan settlement of Tuilasok was the home of Toketok, the man with whom LeGendre had struck agreements in 1867 and 1869. Toketok died in 1873, thus leaving his nephew Tsului to represent Tuilasok in meetings with Saigō Tsugumichi and other foreigners. By Tsului’s side sat Jagarushi Guri Bunkiet—the son of a Tuilasok woman and a Guangdong immigrant surnamed Lin. Bunkiet was born in Checheng or Poliac in 1854 and was purchased by the sonless Toketok, who groomed the bilingual Bunkiet to be a headman.
Bunkiet came to the notice of Qing officials when Hengchun walled city was built in 1875 as a base for Shen Baozhen’s “open the mountains, pacify the indigenes” campaigns.
zh: 排湾族聚落猪朥束是卓杞笃的家乡，李仙得曾于1867年和1869年与此人达成协议。卓杞笃死于1873年，于是留下侄儿楚鲁伊代表猪朥束，与西乡从道及其他外国人会面。楚鲁伊身旁坐着雅加鲁希·古里·文杰——一名猪朥束女子与一位林姓广东移民之子。文杰1854年生于车城或保力，被无子的卓杞笃买下，卓杞笃把双语的文杰培养成头目。
1875年恒春城筑成、作为沈葆桢“开山抚番”征伐的基地时，文杰引起了清朝官员的注意。

en: For his success as a labor recruiter, the Qing awarded Bunkiet the surname Pan. He thereafter worked, presumably as an interpreter, in the 1890s campaigns to pacify the Hengchun tribes, earning a Qing meritorious rank of the fifth order (
zh: 因招募劳力有功，清朝赐文杰潘姓。此后他在1890年代平定恒春诸部落的征伐中效力，大概是充当通译，因功获清廷授予五品官阶（wu-pin）。

en: In November 1895, Bunkiet, bearing a flag his family had received from Saigō twenty-one years earlier, attended Hengchun dispatch-station chief Sagara Nagatsuna’s first official audience.

That same month, a Japanese garrison stationed in Sabaree mistakenly killed several men and burned down even more dwellings. According to one version of the story, the garrison heard shots fired from the direction of a Koalut village. In another version, they mistook an armed contingent of Paiwan men for hostiles. In any event, skittish Japanese troops responded by tying eight villagers to trees. While Koaluts were fleeing, the Japanese proceeded to torch twelve houses. They also shot and killed six residents in the confusion. News of the depredations had spread to neighboring settlements when Bunkiet stepped in. With Bunkiet’s intercession, the Japanese government assuaged local anger by disbursing twenty yen each to the families of the dead and five yen each to the victims of the massacre. For this service, Bunkiet was appointed commissioner attached to the Hengchun dispatch station.
zh: 1895年11月，文杰擎着家族二十一年前从西乡那里领受的一面旗，出席了恒春出张所所长相良长纲的首次正式接见。

同月，驻射麻里的一支日本驻军误杀了数名男子，并烧毁了更多房屋。据故事的一个版本，驻军听到从龟好儿某村方向传来的枪声。另一版本则说，他们把一队武装的排湾男子误当成了敌人。无论如何，神经紧张的日军作出的反应是把八名村民绑在树上。龟好儿人逃散之际，日军接着纵火烧了十二栋房屋，还在混乱中枪杀了六名居民。焚屋杀人的消息传到邻近聚落时，文杰出面介入。经他斡旋，日本政府向死者家属各发放二十日元、向屠杀的受害者各发放五日元，以平息当地的愤怒。因这一功劳，文杰被任命为恒春出张所的嘱托。

en: As the government-general’s new point man for the lower Hengchun, Bunkiet, in concert with other local leaders, brokered the formal submission of forty-four tribes in Taidong that same February.

Bunkiet and another bicultural mediator, a Puyuma woman known to us as Tata Rara, most famously assisted the government-general on May 18, 1896. Instead of merely brokering an agreement, Tata mobilized Paiwan and Puyuma troops to militarily defeat a remnant Qing officer named Liu Deshao (Liu Tek-chok) and his followers.
zh: 作为总督府在下恒春新任的干将，文杰与其他地方首领协同，于同年2月居间促成了台东四十四处部落的正式归顺。
文杰与另一位双文化中介者——我们称之为达达·拉拉的卑南女子——最著名的一次协助总督府，是在1896年5月18日。达达不只是居间促成协议，还动员排湾与卑南的武装，从军事上击败了一名清军残部军官刘德杓（Liu Tek-chok）及其追随者。

en: The Qing formally surrendered Taiwan on April 17, 1895, but (because of numerous rebellions) it took until April 1, 1896, for Japan to officially declare an end to the state of war and institute a civil government. Liu Deshao remained in southern Taiwan, operating as a local potentate beyond the reach of the government-general past the cessation of military rule on the island.

In accord with Shen Baozhen’s “open the mountains, pacify the indigenes” program, the Qing had begun to station officials and soldiers in Taidong (near Beinan) in 1875. Around two thousand men were posted throughout the Hengchun Peninsula. They were not especially brutal, wrote the Japanese commentator Hara Segai, but they did make inspections, conscript labor, and take millet and rice without paying. The Qing government accordingly became loathsome to the people, inciting head-hunting attacks on plainsmen and provoking armed standoffs. According to Hara’s report, when the Japanese took Taiwan in 1895, the Qing abandoned these forces without alerting them of the cession. The remnants resorted to looting and stealing to feed themselves, and the area descended into chaos.
zh: 清朝于1895年4月17日正式割让台湾，但（由于叛乱频发）日本直到1896年4月1日才正式宣布结束战争状态、设立文官政府。刘德杓留在南台湾，在岛上军事统治结束之后，仍以地方豪强的身份行事，超出总督府力所能及的范围。
依照沈葆桢“开山抚番”的方案，清朝自1875年起开始在台东（卑南附近）派驻官员与士兵。约两千人被部署到整个恒春半岛。日本评论者原栖崖写道，他们并不算特别残暴，但确实会巡查、征发劳役，并不付钱就拿走粟米与稻米。清政府因此招致民众憎恶，激起针对平地人的猎首袭击，并引发武装对峙。据原栖崖的报告，1895年日本接管台湾时，清朝抛弃了这些部队，未告知他们割让之事。残部靠劫掠偷盗糊口，该地区陷入混乱。

en: During his first diplomatic mission to Taidong in February 1896, Sagara Nagatsuna consulted with Zhang Yichun, a prominent merchant and husband of the multilingual interpreter Tata Rara. Zhang’s wife, Tata, then lobbied Sagara’s translator, Nakamura Yūsuke, to intervene against Liu’s remnant troops (see
zh: 1896年2月，相良长纲首次出使台东执行外交任务期间，与知名商人张义春商议；张义春是通晓多种语言的通译达达·拉拉的丈夫。张的妻子达达随后游说相良的通译中村雄助，请他出手对付刘的残部（见

en: Tata Rara was the daughter of Chen Ansheng, a chief who dealt with LeGendre during his perambulations in the 1870s. One source even referred to her as “Chen Tata.”
Tata Rara spoke Southern Min Chinese, as well as the Puyuma, Paiwanese, and Amis languages. Like Bunkiet, she earned a salary of six yuan per month as a Qing subofficial,
presumably for services rendered during the
campaigns.
zh: 达达·拉拉是陈安生之女；陈安生是一位头目，1870年代李仙得巡行期间曾与他打交道。一份史料甚至称她为“陈达达”。
达达·拉拉会说闽南语，以及卑南语、排湾语和阿美语。与文杰一样，她作为清朝佐杂官每月领六元薪水，
大概是酬劳她在开山抚番征伐中所出的力。

en: In May 1896, Tata and Bunkiet organized a militia of three hundred indigenes to expel the Qing remnants. Tata Rara herself personally led the men through a hail of musket fire to secure the surrender of a thousand Qing troops. She appears to have been a formidable commander. One German publication referred to her as the “Puyuma Joan of Arc,” while a Japanese report referred to her as a “heroine” (see
zh: 1896年5月，达达与文杰组织了一支由三百名原住民组成的民兵队伍，去驱逐清军残部。达达·拉拉亲自率领众人冒着密集的滑膛枪火，迫使一千名清军投降。她似乎是一位令人生畏的指挥官。一份德国出版物称她为“卑南圣女贞德”，而一份日本报告则称她为“女杰”（见

Tata Rara belatedly received her reward of forty yen on February 9, 1900.

en: After the suppression of Liu Deshao, Bunkiet and Sagara Nagatsuna applied to have the colony’s first Japanese-language institute built for indigenous students. On September 2, 1896, a plan to build this modest school was approved. Bunkiet then mobilized his followers to supply land, building materials, and labor in time for a September 10 opening ceremony. One encomium to Bunkiet reports that he registered his own nephew to lead by example and that over thirty youths in Tuilasok followed suit.
A less celebratory account by a Japanese teacher reported that the first group of twenty-seven students did not know why they had matriculated, except that the headman Bunkiet had sent them.
zh: 平定刘德杓之后，文杰与相良长纲申请为原住民学生兴建殖民地第一所国语传习所。1896年9月2日，兴建这所简陋学校的计划获批。文杰随即动员追随者提供土地、建材与劳力，赶在9月10日的开学典礼前备齐。一篇颂扬文杰的文字记载，他送自己的侄儿报名以身作则，猪朥束三十多名青年随之效仿。
一位日本教师不那么颂扬的记述则说，第一批二十七名学生并不知道自己为何入学，只晓得是头目文杰把他们送来的。

en: Three neighboring Hengchun Paiwan settlements, Koro, Tekiri, and Kauwan, responded to Sagara’s announcement of the “urgent matter” of Japanese-language education with much less enthusiasm. They temporized by convening councils to deliberate the matter. Tekiri and Kauwan did not apply for schools, and by 1900, only two institutes had been built in all of Hengchun. Koro village finally applied on the condition that the school be combined with a gun and ammunition depot. As Kitamura points out, the language institutes were not gifts from the government but were built with locally provided materials and labor. “Buy-in” could not be assumed. Several Paiwan schools were shut down temporarily or closed because of armed attacks from neighboring settlements.

Reminiscent of the Meiji state’s early efforts to spread compulsory schooling throughout Japan, central ambitions outstripped budgets, parents could not always spare the foregone labor of the children in the fields, and resentment by locals who paid for these unfunded mandates led to hundreds of cases of vandalism.
zh: 恒春邻近的三处排湾聚落——科罗、特基里与考万——对相良宣布的日语教育这件“急务”，反应冷淡得多。他们召集会议商议此事，借以拖延。特基里与考万没有申请设校，到1900年，整个恒春只建起两所传习所。科罗村最终提出申请，条件是学校须与一座枪械弹药库合设。正如北村所指出的，这些传习所并非政府的馈赠，而是用地方提供的材料与劳力建成的。政府并不能想当然地指望各社同意并出力。好几所排湾学校因邻近聚落的武装袭击而暂时停办或关闭。
这令人想起明治国家早期在全日本推行义务教育的努力：中央的雄心超出了预算，父母未必舍得放弃孩子在田里本该付出的劳力，而为这些未由中央拨款的办学要求承担费用的当地人心生怨恨，导致数百起毁损公物的事件。

en: Despite these hiccups, the lower Hengchun villages were far ahead of indigenous settlements in the north in terms of formal education.

We recall here that Ōkubo Toshimichi’s parting shots to Qing officials in Beijing at the conclusion of his negotiations in 1874 included criticism of the lack of schools in the Paiwan settlements in Langqiao. While the Qing did not exactly dot the landscape with schoolhouses, it did make a beginning. After Japanese forces left in 1874, Hengchun city drew population by decree but also through attraction, as the Qing filled in an administrative grid with
(mutual responsibility) units and

(administrative villages). Educational institutions to transform indigenous peoples into Sinophone Qing subjects were also piloted. This flurry of activity directed at horizontal integration tipped the balance of power in favor of the Han, vis-à-vis the formerly dominant Paiwan, during the twenty-year interval between the Taiwan Expedition and the assumption of Japanese rule.
zh: 尽管有这些小波折，下恒春各村在正规教育方面仍远远领先于北部的原住民聚落。

我们在此回想，大久保利通1874年谈判结束时在北京对清朝官员的临别抨击，就包括批评琅峤排湾聚落缺乏学校。清朝虽谈不上遍设学堂，却确实开了个头。1874年日军撤离后，恒春城既靠政令、也靠吸引来聚拢人口，清朝以保甲（连带责任）单位与庄（行政村）填满了行政网格。把原住民改造为讲汉语的清国臣民的教育机构也进行了试点。在侵台之役与日本接管统治之间这二十年里，这一连串旨在横向整合的活动，使力量天平相对于此前占优势的排湾人，倒向了汉人一边。

en: When Inō Kanori arrived in Hengchun at the behest of the TGG education bureau, the Tuilasok annex school was already in operation. In late October 1898, Inō stopped in the walled city, visited the local Pacification Office, and finally reached Tuilasok. During his tour, Bunkiet invited Inō into a ceramic-roofed home, well appointed with Chinese furniture. Bunkiet put on an elaborate feast for his Japanese guests and showed Inō a treasured copy of the admonition that Saigō Tsugumichi had issued in 1874, warning the Paiwan to be obedient to the Qing.
zh: 伊能嘉矩奉台湾总督府学务局之命抵达恒春时，猪朥束分校场已在运作。1898年10月下旬，伊能在城内停留，走访了当地抚垦署，最终抵达猪朥束。巡视期间，文杰请伊能进了一栋瓦顶房屋，屋内中式家具陈设齐整。文杰为日本客人摆下丰盛宴席，并向伊能展示了一份珍藏的谕示副本——那是西乡从道1874年颁布、告诫排湾人服从清朝的文书。

en: In his synthetic report on conditions throughout Taiwan’s interior, Inō wrote that the lower Hengchun towns such as Tuilasok were the most “advanced” of all indigenous peoples, due to frequent intermarriage with Chinese in their proximity. Inō singled out Tuilasok and Sabaree especially as places where tiled-roof homes and the use of Chinese language were common—these villages were, in fact, hardly distinguishable from Han settlements, according to Inō. The “lower Hengchun tribes,” south of the line stretching from Mudan to Fenggang (see
), were therefore geographically advantaged compared to the more isolated and less “advanced” upper Hengchun villages, according to Inō’s evolutionary taxonomy.

After the Qing began to fund reclamation and Han migration, the southernmost Paiwan tribes, such as Sabaree, Tuilasok, and Koalut, were forced to adopt the Qing hairstyle, the queue. In the northern part of the peninsula, however, around Mudan and Kuskus, Paiwan men retained their Paiwan hairstyles.
zh: 伊能在关于台湾内陆各地状况的综合报告中写道，猪朥束等下恒春市镇是所有原住民中最“先进”的，因为他们与近旁汉人频繁通婚。伊能特别举出猪朥束与射麻里，说那里瓦顶房屋与汉语的使用都很普遍——据伊能看，这些村子实际上与汉人聚落几乎无从区分。因此，按伊能的进化论分类，位于牡丹至枫港一线以南的“下恒春部落”（见
），在地理上比更孤立、更不“先进”的上恒春各村占优势。
清朝开始资助开垦与汉人移民后，最南端的排湾部落，如射麻里、猪朥束与龟好儿，被迫留起清朝发式——辫发。然而在半岛北部、牡丹与高士佛一带，排湾男子仍保留排湾发式。

en: In 1902 the Japanese Hengchun district officer applied to abolish the status of Mudan, Kuskus, Sabaree, and Tuilasok as “savage villages” (Japanese
, Chinese
) and promote them to “townships” (Japanese shō, Chinese

). The application, like Inō’s survey ethnography, noted in-migration of Han and Paiwanese acculturation and intermarriage with Han as factors in favor of township status. Another reason the lower Hengchun tribes qualified for “normal administration” was their cultural competence regarding private property and the conduct of commerce. Most notably, unlike indigenous peoples more generally, the lower Hengchun Sinicized indigenes understood how to calculate the worth of trade-goods in abstract monetary units—rather than in terms of customary equivalences in bartered goods (see chapter 3). In a similar vein, the application noted that lower Hengchun Paiwanese adjudicated disputes through mediation. They did not follow formal court proceedings, but at least disputes were not solved by feuds, vendettas, or divination.
zh: 1902年，日本恒春厅长申请废除牡丹、高士佛、射麻里与猪朥束作为“番社”（日语 sha，汉语 she）的身份，把它们升格为“庄”（日语 shō，汉语 zhuang）。这份申请与伊能的调查民族志一样，举出汉人迁入、排湾人的涵化以及与汉人通婚，作为支持升格为庄的因素。下恒春部落够格实行“普通行政”的另一理由，是他们在私有财产与商业经营方面的文化能力。最显著的是，与一般原住民不同，下恒春已汉化的原住民懂得用抽象货币单位计算贸易货物的价值——而不是按以物易物的习惯等价来计算（见第3章）。同样，申请指出下恒春排湾人通过调解裁断纠纷。他们不遵循正式法庭程序，但至少纠纷不是靠世仇、血仇复仇或占卜来解决的。

en: As a surplus-producing, stockbreeding, and agricultural area, lower Hengchun, it was argued, should contribute to the cost of government by paying taxes—which meant extending all rights and obligations of colonial subjects (hontōjin) to Koalut, Sabaree, Tuilasok, and selected other villages. Thus, on April 28, 1904, the former abodes of Isa, Toketok, and the wreckers of the
were, administratively speaking, no longer “savage” in the eyes of the Japanese government.
Bunkiet himself is said to have led a group of Paiwan residents out of the mixed-residence Tuilasok to resettle in Mudan Bay in 1901.
zh: 作为一个出产剩余、畜牧兼农业的地区，据称下恒春应当纳税以分担政府开销——这意味着把殖民臣民（本岛人，hontōjin）的一切权利与义务扩展到龟好儿、射麻里、猪朥束及若干其他村落。于是，1904年4月28日，伊萨、卓杞笃以及罗妹号劫掠者的旧居，就行政而言，在日本政府眼中已不再“野蛮”。
据说文杰本人曾于1901年带领一批排湾居民离开杂居的猪朥束，迁往牡丹湾重新定居。

en: The evidence offered above suggests that Japan’s “savage border,” reckoned as a cultural boundary that separated economic moderns from indigenous peoples, reflected the extent of the Qing government’s reach by 1895: wherever Paiwanese had been forced to wear the queue, normal administration followed. In fact, the lower Hengchun settlements of Mudan and Kuskus (the villages whose men reportedly did not wear the Qing queue), located just north of Sabaree, Tuilasok, and Koalut, remained classified as
(savage settlements) well into the 1930s. As
and

indicate, Japan’s ethnic classification excluded Tuilasok, Koalut, and Sabaree from the Paiwan zone by 1912, while most of lower Hengchun remained firmly within it. The colorful maps attached to 1930s statistical compendia followed suit. On the Paiwan side, as late as 1934, Mudan and Kuskus were still sending children to the “aborigine schools,”

despite the region’s status as a relatively wealthy and economically developed location. Thanks to its suitable riverbanks, Mudan became an early site for the cultivation of paddy rice in 1909. Within a couple of decades, Mudan was a model rice-production center,
though it still remained within the indigenous zone.
zh: 上面提供的证据表明，日本的“生番界”被视为一道把经济上的现代人与原住民分隔开来的文化边界，它反映了1895年清朝政府势力所及的范围：凡排湾人被迫留辫发之处，后来便实行普通行政。事实上，位于射麻里、猪朥束与龟好儿正北方的下恒春聚落牡丹与高士佛（据报其男子不留清朝辫发的村子），直到1930年代仍被归为“番社”（sha）。如
与
所示，到1912年，日本的族群分类已把猪朥束、龟好儿与射麻里排除在排湾区之外，而下恒春的大部分仍牢牢处于其中。1930年代统计汇编所附的彩色地图也如法炮制。在排湾一侧，迟至1934年，牡丹与高士佛仍把孩子送进“蕃人学校”，
尽管该地区相对富裕、经济发达。得益于适宜的河岸，牡丹于1909年成为早期水稻种植地。不出二十年，牡丹已是模范稻米生产中心，
却仍留在原住民区之内。

en: This seemingly arbitrary line—which divided fellow Paiwanese in a surplus-producing and fertile area of Taiwan into normally and specially administered peoples—had one important consequence. Like the qualifications for indigenous-district policemen (see chapter 1), which were lower than those for policemen stationed in Han districts, the indigenous school curriculum was adapted to special conditions—it was watered down. From the beginning, indigenous students were not expected to perform as well as their Han counterparts in Hengchun city or the other common schools and language institutes. Even under auspicious conditions—with an eager and powerful collaborator in Bunkiet and a surplus-producing Paiwan population versed in the Southern Min dialect of Chinese—Sagara Nagatsuna and the higher-ups in Taipei designed the Tuilasok annex school to keep Hengchun residents of Paiwan ancestry “down on the farm.” Although it has been celebrated as the first indigenous education facility in the history of Japanese colonial rule, the Tuilasok annex was, in fact, a precursor to the third-tier educational system that would define Japanese rule in the highlands.
zh: 这条看似武断的界线——把台湾一处出产剩余、土地肥沃地区里的排湾同胞划分为分别由普通行政与特别行政管辖的两类人——有一个重要后果。正如原住民地区警察的资格（见第1章）低于派驻汉人地区的警察，原住民学校的课程也被调整以适应特殊条件——它被打折扣了。从一开始，人们就不指望原住民学生表现得与恒春城或其他公学校、传习所里的汉人同龄人一样好。即便在有利条件下——有文杰这样热心而有力的合作者，有一群出产剩余、通晓闽南语方言的排湾人——相良长纲与台北的上峰仍把猪朥束分校场设计成让有排湾血统的恒春居民“困守田园”。虽然它被誉为日本殖民统治史上第一所原住民教育设施，猪朥束分校场实际上却是日后界定日本山地统治的第三等级教育体制的先声。

en: By March 1898 the Taiwan Government-General had built sixteen Japanese-language training institutes and an additional thirty-six annex schools; four of the latter were for indigenous children (all in Taidong or Hengchun, in the south). That same year, the institutes were discontinued and replaced by a more ambitious common-school (kōgakkō) system. Its six-year curriculum “consisted of ethics, Japanese language, classical Chinese (composition, reading, calligraphy), arithmetic, music and gymnastics.”

However, in two locations, Hengchun and Taidong, the vocationally oriented institutes were left in place until 1905. As one official report put it, the “reason is not far to seek. The existence of so many aborigines in these districts accounts for this exception.”
In 1904, thirteen language institutes and annexes served indigenous children, with an enrollment of 803 (759 males and 44 females).
zh: 到1898年3月，台湾总督府已建起十六所国语传习所，另有三十六所分校场；后者中有四所是为原住民儿童设的（全在南部的台东或恒春）。同年，传习所被停办，代之以一套更宏大的公学校（kōgakkō）体制。其六年制课程“包括修身、日语、汉文（作文、阅读、书法）、算术、音乐与体操”。
然而在恒春与台东两地，职业导向的传习所被保留到1905年。正如一份官方报告所言，“理由不难想见。这些地区存在如此多的原住民，正是这一例外的缘由。”
1904年，有十三所传习所与分校场服务于原住民儿童，在学人数803人（男759人，女44人）。

en: Even after the remnant language institutes for indigenous children were discontinued in 1905, indigenous schools remained separate and inferior, but under the new name aborigine common schools (banjin kōgakkō).

The government-general’s own English-language propaganda was forthright: “According to the new [1905] arrangement, the school course covers only four years instead of six... while the number of subjects was made less than those of the [common schools]. The aborigine pupils have in the regular course only three subjects: Morals, Japanese, and Arithmetic. They have no need of Chinese classics, Science, and Commerce. Only Agriculture, Manual Training, and Singing (one or all three) may be added to the regular course of study according to the intellectual development of the tribe.”
zh: 即便1905年残存的原住民儿童传习所被停办之后，原住民学校依旧分离而低劣，只是换了个新名字——蕃人公学校（banjin kōgakkō）。
总督府自己的英文宣传直言不讳：“依照新的〔1905〕安排，学制只涵盖四年而非六年……科目数目也少于〔公学校〕。蕃人学生在正科中只有三门科目：修身、日语与算术。他们不需要汉文经典、理科与商业。只有农业、手工与唱歌（其一或全部三者）可依该部落的智力发展程度加入正科。”

en: Because the residents of Tuilasok, Sabaree, and Koalut bore the burden of taxation after their incorporation into the regularly administered territory, their children were theoretically eligible to attend six-year common schools with a full curriculum.

Aborigine common schools were built among Amis and Paiwan peoples who lived under normal administration and remained concentrated in the “advanced” south and the eastern rift valley into the 1930s. By 1935, there were exceptions: five aborigine common schools had been built in the specially administered territories. Of these five, only one was located in the north among the Atayal, Sediq, and Truku populations.
zh: 由于猪朥束、射麻里与龟好儿的居民在被并入普通行政区后承担了纳税义务，他们的孩子理论上够格进入课程齐全的六年制公学校。
蕃人公学校建在实行普通行政的阿美与排湾人中间，直到1930年代仍集中在“先进”的南部与东部纵谷。到1935年出现了例外：特别行政区内已建起五所蕃人公学校。这五所中，只有一所位于北部泰雅、赛德克与德路固人中间。

en: Eika Tai has noted that the common schools for Han children were aimed at creating “citizens” (

), whereas that term was absent in planning documents and curriculum for the indigenous common schools. This nomenclature reflected the government-general’s pre-1930s approach to indigenous education: it would create not fellow nationals but rather docile and useful subjects.
zh: 戴英华指出，为汉人儿童设立的公学校旨在造就“国民”（kokumin），而这个词在原住民公学校的规划文件与课程中却付之阙如。这一用语反映了总督府1930年代之前对原住民教育的方针：它要造就的不是同胞国民，而是驯顺而有用的臣民。

en: THE EXPANSION OF INDIGENOUS EDUCATION TO THE NORTH
zh: 原住民教育向北部的扩展

en: Due to the violence surrounding the camphor wars, which surely fed into Japanese officialdom’s low estimation of Atayal cultural capacity, the first “northern tribes” school was established in Quchi in 1908. The Quchi school was called an aborigine youth school (bandō kyōikujo), a new institution that complemented the aborigine common schools. The youth schools were creatures of the guardline movements discussed in chapter 1. In contrast to schools for Han, making “citizens” was not part of their writ.
zh: 由于樟脑战争伴随的暴力——它无疑助长了日本官方对泰雅族文化能力的低估——第一所“北部部落”学校于1908年在屈尺设立。屈尺学校称为蕃童教育所（bandō kyōikujo），是一种与蕃人公学校相辅相成的新机构。这些教育所是第1章所讨论的隘勇线推进的产物。与汉人学校相反，造就“国民”不在它们的职责范围之内。

en: At the Quchi school and others like it, indigenous children were taught comportment (bowing, sitting respectfully, interacting with superiors), lifestyle “improvement” (wearing geta [clog-sandals], using chopsticks, wearing pants), ethics (loyalty), farming (intensive, fixed plot), and handicraft production (see

). The youth schools were staffed by policemen and district-office staffers. The guidelines were drawn up in 1908, in the midst of the war against northern indigenes. They were built in part to win over the indigenous peoples and also to train interpreters.

The pioneering Quchi school was moved upriver to Wulai in 1911. The bulk of instruction was in field cultivation, tree felling, and other “regular employments. Japanese-language training was the second most important pursuit.”
zh: 在屈尺学校及类似机构里，原住民儿童被教授举止（鞠躬、恭敬地坐、与上级打交道）、生活“改良”（穿木屐（geta）、用筷子、穿裤子）、伦理（忠诚）、农耕（集约、定耕）与手工业生产（见
）。教育所由警察与厅署职员充任师资。指南于1908年对北部原住民作战正酣之际拟定。设立它们，部分是为了笼络原住民，也是为了训练通译。

en: In 1915, the same year that Japan’s major military offensives against indigenous peoples were terminated with the retirement of Sakuma Samata, the Taiwan Government-General issued first-year and second-year readers for indigenous children titled
(A reader for indigenes).
A user’s manual for

(published in 1916) forecasted an ethnically bifurcated administration and the birth of indigeneity in modern Taiwan. Taiwan’s educational administrators in effect hardened the line that LeGendre drew between indigenes and Han for political purposes in 1872 (see chapter 1), that census-bureau desk jockeys inscribed between “Mongolians” and “Malays” in 1905, and that guardline architects scorched into the earth in the 1910s. The manual explained:
zh: 1915年，正是日本对原住民的主要军事攻势随佐久间左马太卸任而告终的那一年，台湾总督府为原住民儿童发行了题为《蕃人读本》（Banjin dokuhon）的一年级与二年级读本。
一本《蕃人读本》使用手册（1916年出版）预示了一种按族群分叉的行政，以及现代台湾原住民身份的诞生。台湾的教育行政官实际上固化了这样一条界线：李仙得1872年出于政治目的在原住民与汉人之间划下的那条（见第1章），普查局案头官僚1905年在“蒙古人种”与“马来人种”之间铭刻的那条，以及隘勇线规划者1910年代以焦土烙入大地的那条。手册解释道：

en: In April 1914... aborigine common school regulations were promulgated, beginning a new chapter in indigenous education. [Initially...], the aborigine common schools used the Ministry of Education elementary-school reader designed for

(Japanese), or the Taiwan Government-General common-school reader for hontōjin (Han Taiwanese).... However, it goes without saying that these two readers were inappropriate for aborigines, who are of a different race, who differ in language, whose environment and climate is not the same, and whose lifestyles and cultures are varied. Therefore, the government-general ordered the formation of an editorial board for a new set of
zh: 1914年4月……颁布了蕃人公学校规程，开启了原住民教育的新篇章。〔起初……〕蕃人公学校使用文部省为内地人（日本人）设计的小学读本，或台湾总督府为本岛人（台湾汉人）编写的公学校读本……然而，不言而喻，这两种读本都不适合原住民——他们属于不同的种族，语言有别，环境与气候不同，生活方式与文化也各异。因此，总督府下令组建一套新《蕃人读本》的编辑委员会……

en: While this manifesto suggests that indigenes had varied cultures and lifestyles, it was premised on the notion that they were all subunits of a Malay race that was also inscribed in the 1905 census categories. Education bureaucrats thus based the different levels of education, for Han and indigenous Taiwanese, on perduring attributes such as environment, race, and culture. The phrasing of the guidelines amplifies Matsuoka Tadasu’s view that 1915 was the turning point when Japanese colonists began to accept the specially administered territory as a permanent, rather than expedient, division.
zh: 虽然这份宣言暗示原住民拥有各异的文化与生活方式，它却以一个观念为前提：他们全都是马来人种的亚单位，而这一人种也被铭刻在1905年的普查类别中。教育官僚于是把汉人与台湾原住民的不同教育层级，建立在环境、种族、文化等持久属性之上。指南的措辞印证了松冈达的看法：1915年是转折点，日本殖民者自此开始把特别行政区接受为一种永久性的、而非权宜性的划分。

en: In 1902, by contrast, the district officer of Hengchun applied to move Tuilasok, Sabaree, and Koalut under normal administration ostensibly because these communities had been
. However, Sinicized referred to those who spoke Minnan Chinese (a Fujianese tongue) and wore a Central Asian hairstyle (the Qing queue). Therefore, the term

in this case did not have an ethnic referent but served as a proxy for the ability to produce surplus wealth and participate in a commodified economy. We can read this circa 1904 usage of Han as equivalent to
(good subject), an old Qing term that separated most imperial subjects from pariahs, bannermen, nobles, and outlanders.
zh: 相比之下，1902年恒春厅长申请把猪朥束、射麻里与龟好儿划归普通行政，表面上是因为这些社群已经汉化。然而，“汉化”指的是那些说闽南语（一种福建方言）、留中亚发式（清朝辫发）的人。因此，此处的“汉人”一词并无族群指涉，而是充当了一种替代指标，衡量的是生产剩余财富、参与商品化经济的能力。我们可以把这种约1904年对“汉人”的用法，读作等同于“良民”（liangmin）——一个清朝旧词，把大多数帝国臣民与贱民、旗人、贵族及化外之民区分开来。

en: But under the 1916 educational guidelines for indigenes, reflecting wider currents in the post–World War I Wilsonian dispensation, indigenous status was being moved out of the plastic category of “uncivilized” and into the static category of “possessing unique attributes” as a racial/cultural marker, while the term

moved in the same direction as it also became particularized as an ethnonym. As Sakano Tōru has argued, the first decades of Japanese colonial rule saw a conflation of “civilization” with “Sinicization” in the discourse on “aborigine improvement.” However, by the 1930s, “imperialization/Japanification” had become firmly entrenched as the telos of progress in official discourse.
zh: 但在1916年原住民教育指南之下——它反映了第一次世界大战后威尔逊式秩序的更广泛潮流——原住民身份正被移出“未开化”这一可塑范畴，移入“具有独特属性”这一作为种族／文化标记的固定范畴；与此同时，“汉人”一词也朝同一方向移动，同样被特殊化为一个族名。正如坂野彻所论，日本殖民统治的头几十年，在“原住民改良”的话语中把“文明”与“汉化”混为一谈。然而到1930年代，“皇民化／日本化”已牢固确立为官方话语中进步的终极目标。

en: The pointed suppression of Chinese-character (Japanese
, Chinese
) use in the 1915 readers furthered the ethnic bifurcation of Taiwan into Han and indigenous moieties. While common schools for Han students
and late Qing indigene schools in Taiwan focused on Chinese reading and writing,

Japanese authorities in post-Sakuma Taiwan regarded Chinese characters as optional for indigenes, almost a luxury. The first two years of indigenous instruction, according to reformed rules, were conducted in katakana (a syllabary). Teachers stressed oral communication and diction; hiragana (another syllabary) was added in the third year, with some very elementary Chinese characters. In the fourth year, indigenes learned a few dozen
related to their customs, surroundings, and vocations but not nearly enough to read a Japanese newspaper or a Chinese poem.
zh: 1915年读本中对汉字（日语 kanji，汉语 hanzi）使用的刻意压制，进一步强化了台湾社会在汉人与原住民之间的两分。汉人学生的公学校
与清末台湾的原住民学校都侧重汉文读写，
而后佐久间时代台湾的日本当局却把汉字视为原住民可有可无的东西，几乎是一种奢侈。按改革后的规则，原住民教学的头两年用片假名（一种音节文字）进行。教师强调口头沟通与发音；第三年加入平假名（另一种音节文字），外加一些极浅显的汉字。第四年，原住民学几十个与他们的习俗、环境、职业相关的汉字，但远不足以读懂一份日本报纸或一首汉诗。

en: Of course, Japanese itself, like Chinese, was hardly a monolith, and what constituted Japanese in 1915 required spelling out. Because many indigenous-district policemen hailed from northeastern Japan and Kyūshū, the 1916 teacher’s guide, echoing those for “national-language” teachers in the home islands, mandated the use of Tokyo-standard pronunciations. It inveighed against the rural Japanese policemen’s “ragged Japanese” and “vulgar colloquialisms” and “mispronunciations,” and it urged proper diction.
Shimoyama Jihei’s son recalled that the Kyūshūans and Okinawans who staffed the aborigine police passed their rough Japanese on to their students; female Atayal women commonly used locutions like
and
(very casual forms of male speech).
zh: 当然，日语本身与汉语一样，绝非铁板一块，1915年何谓日语需要明确界定。由于许多原住民地区警察来自日本东北与九州，1916年的教师指南呼应本土诸岛“国语”教师的指南，规定使用东京标准音。它抨击乡村日本警察的“粗陋日语”“粗俗口语”与“误读”，并敦促规范的发音。
下山治平的儿子回忆说，充任蕃人警察的九州人与冲绳人把他们粗粝的日语传给了学生；泰雅女子普遍使用诸如“俺”（ore）与“你”（o mae）之类的说法（男性言语中极随便的形式）。

en: Again promoting ethnic bifurcation, Japanese educators also pushed the notion that, as members of the Malay race, the indigenes were ethnic affines of the Japanese. Teachers could use the fourth-year reader’s account of the emperor Jimmu’s eastward conquests, it was suggested, to incline Taiwan’s “Malays” (indigenes) to disidentify with the Han race and imagine themselves as long-lost cousins of the Yamato (Japanese) ethnos.
zh: 日本教育者再次推动族群分叉，还灌输这样一种观念：作为马来人种的成员，原住民是日本人的族群姻亲。有人建议，教师可以利用四年级读本中神武天皇东征的记述，使台湾的“马来人”（原住民）倾向于不认同汉人种族，并把自己想象成大和（日本）民族失散已久的表亲。

en: So while the emphasis of indigenous education was practical and focused on everyday conversation, it also held within it the seeds of more complex forms of indoctrination. The fourth-grade reader taught students that a typical
(aborigine settlement) contained about 30 families and 150 residents. Indigenous residents generally farmed their plots but occasionally hunted in the mountains. Within each

, two buildings were most prominent: the schoolhouse and the police station. According to the reader, before the police station arrived, farming was difficult because indigenous peoples were in a perpetual state of war. Now they could farm peacefully. And, if they studied hard enough in school, they might be sent to the capital to study Japanese. One sample lesson reproduced postcards from a fictitious older brother in Taipei. The postcards reproduced pictures of the governor-general’s residence and a large, ornate school building, as well. In addition to the large buildings of the capital, the reader also illustrated the countless thousands of Japanese troops that paraded in Tokyo and stood ready to put down rebellious imperial subjects.

In short, the reader reproduced in miniature the cardinal lessons of the indigenous sightseeing tours to Taipei and Tokyo, wherein headmen were made to understand imperial might and wealth and, hopefully, were dissuaded from further rebellious activity.
zh: 因此，原住民教育虽然侧重实用、聚焦日常会话，其内部却也埋下了更复杂灌输形式的种子。四年级读本教学生说，一处典型的番社（ban-sha，原住民聚落）约有30户、150名居民。原住民居民一般耕种自己的田地，偶尔进山打猎。每处番社内，有两栋建筑最显眼：学堂与警察驻在所。据读本说，在警察驻在所到来之前，农耕很困难，因为原住民处于无休止的战争状态。如今他们可以安心耕作了。而且，如果他们在学校足够用功，还可能被送到台北去学日语。一篇示范课文复制了台北一位虚构兄长寄来的明信片。明信片也复制了总督官邸与一栋宏大华丽校舍的图片。除了首都的高大建筑，读本还描绘了成千上万在东京列队、随时准备镇压叛逆帝国臣民的日本军队。
简言之，读本以微缩形式复制了原住民赴台北、东京观光巡览的核心教训：让头目们领略帝国的威力与财富，并但愿由此打消他们继续叛逆的念头。

en: On the one hand, after 1928, some institutes adopted more challenging curricula. Thereafter, making
(citizens) was a stated goal of indigenous schooling. Chinese characters were now part of the curriculum, as well.

However, proposals to send professional teachers to the indigenous territory, either to sharpen and reinforce the education outlined above or to improve the lives of indigenes, were continually thwarted. Indigenous schools were staffed by policemen for the duration of colonial rule. Throughout the 1920s, enrollments in aborigine youth schools actually increased. Nonetheless, allocations for instructional materials and physical plant were routinely diverted to fund shortfalls elsewhere in the colonial budget. In the end, writes Kitamura Kae, most Japanese-language schools for indigenous peoples, with the exception of the demonstration school at Jiaobanshan (see
), became thinly disguised work camps.
zh: 一方面，1928年之后，一些机构采用了更具挑战性的课程。此后，造就国民（kokumin）成了原住民学校教育的明示目标。汉字也纳入了课程。
然而，向原住民领土派遣专业教师的提议——无论是为了强化上述教育，还是为了改善原住民的生活——却屡屡受挫。整个殖民统治期间，原住民学校都由警察充任师资。1920年代，蕃童教育所的在学人数实际上增加了。尽管如此，教学材料与校舍设备的拨款却常被挪用，去填补殖民预算别处的亏空。北村嘉惠写道，到头来，除角板山的示范学校（见
）外，大多数面向原住民的日语学校都成了几乎不加掩饰的劳动营。
